title: Scorpion sting — Parabuthus severity grade & SA STG action

sources.title: STG & EML Hospital Level Adults, 6th ed. 2024 (updated Mar 2026)
STG & EML Paediatric Hospital Level, 5th ed. 2023 (updated Mar 2026)
Müller GJ, Modler H, Wium CA, Veale DJH. Scorpion sting in southern Africa: diagnosis and management. CME 2012;30(10):356–361
Tomlinson H, Elston DM. What's eating you? The South African fattail scorpion revisited. Cutis 2019;104(4):217–219 (4-grade scale)

dagger_note: † = not in the SA STG (non-STG source named). Grades are not in the STG; the STG gives antivenom only for systemic neurotoxic effects.

items.label: I
items.t: Pain and paraesthesia at the sting site; usually no local inflammation

action.t: Analgesia: lidocaine 1–2% 2 mL local, ice, paracetamol · observe ≥ 12 h

items.label: II
items.t: Local symptoms + remote pain / paraesthesia radiating up the limb

action.t: As grade I · observe ≥ 12 h · generalised paraesthesia + autonomic signs = systemic → treat as III

items.label: III
items.t: Cranial nerve (ptosis, dysphagia, drooling) OR somatic neuromuscular dysfunction (tremor, jerking, weakness) ± autonomic

action.t: Scorpion antivenom 10 mL · continuous respiratory monitoring

items.label: IV
items.t: BOTH cranial nerve AND somatic neuromuscular dysfunction, with autonomic dysfunction

interpretation_stg.t: Observe all thick-tailed (or unidentified) stings ≥ 12 h; monitor respiratory function
Antivenom ONLY for systemic neurotoxic effects
Adult: 10 mL in 100 mL NaCl 0.9% / D5W over 10 min; response slow, may repeat
Child: 10 mL slow IV over 3–5 min (same dose)
Never give antivenom unless ready for anaphylaxis
Cramps: Ca gluconate 10% 10 mL over 10 min, repeat once (max 2 g) · child 0.5 mL/kg slow, ECG
Tetanus toxoid 0.5 mL IM if > 5 y

notes.t: Thick tail + small pincers = Parabuthus (dangerous); thin tail + large pincers = local pain only
Severity usually evident within 15–60 min; adults may be delayed up to 8 h
Children: respiratory failure within 1–2 h; extreme restlessness = severe
Antivenom peaks at 2–6 h — support breathing meanwhile; observe 6–12 h after
Müller 2012: antivenom for ALL systemic envenoming (STG: neurotoxic only)
Hypertension, sweating, visual disturbance = P. granulatus sympathetic storm
